questions.stem: What did the woman do last Tuesday?
questions.stemZh: 这位女士上周二做了什么?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago. I made it clear it was an urgent matter and please send someone as soon as possible. 我上周二跟你们那边一位女士通过话，到现在已经十天了。我讲得很清楚这是急事，请尽快 派人来。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 时间锚 last Tuesday 后的应答。女士主动说 I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday，这里 的 last Tuesday 正对上题干的时间锚，紧跟的动作 spoke to a lady there（there 指上文 男士提到的 central office）就是她那天做的事，这就是答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday ↔Called the man's company 通话沟通改写成打电话给公司

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 选项盗用了对话开头出现的 computer technician 一词，但她见到这位技术员是今天上门 这一刻，并非上周二；上周二她做的是打电话，时间对不上，属答非所问。 借用原文：I'm the computer technician B) 张冠李戴 上周二她是给公司打电话，电话那头是 a lady，而男士本人这周才接到任务上门，上周二两 人根本没接触，把通话对象说成 the man 是张冠李戴。 借用原文：I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday D) 原词陷阱 选项盗用男士自报的 Alpha Maintenance，但那是他工作的公司名，女士只是打电话过 去，并没有亲自上门拜访，visited 这个动作无中生有。 借用原文：I work for Alpha Maintenance

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I'm sorry, but I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics. I simply do not know. All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could. 抱歉，调度安排不归我管，我确实不清楚。我能告诉你的就是，我这周接到电话，已经尽快 赶过来了。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问者的直接应答句 All I can tell you is。女士追问他能不能早点来，男士的应答里 All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could 用 All I can tell you is 把重点框出来，这句他亲口交代自己接电话后的动作，是答案句。

analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 选项的 in charge 直接盗用原文 I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics，但原文是 否定，他强调调度不归他负责、自己也不清楚，根本没说去请示负责人，正好与原文相反。 借用原文：I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics C) 张冠李戴 central office 来自男士早先的推测 someone from your office called our central office，那是女方办公室的人打给总部，不是他接电话后做的；把别人的动作安到他头上， 是张冠李戴。 借用原文：someone from your office called our central office D) 原词陷阱 designated an engineer 盗用 I'm the engineer designated to your case，那是他猜测 自己被指派的过程、动作发出方是公司，不是他本人接电话后所为，属答非所问。 借用原文：I'm the engineer designated to your case

analysis.label: 定位

analysis.label: 信号

analysis.label: 定位

analysis.text: 一问一答的指代承接。男士先问 Do you know if it's backed up?，他随后解释 it 指 its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else；女士最后说 My manager would know，这句 would know 承接的正是前面备份这个问题，所以经理会知道的就是有 没有备份。

analysis.text: Do you know if it's backed up? ↔Whether the contents have been backed up if it's backed up 改写成 whether…backed up

M: 你对学习法律有更多想法了吗？ 2 W: I've been thinking about it a lot, yes. In fact, this is why I wished to speak to you. I wanted to hear more about what it's like. W: 我一直在认真考虑，是的。实际上，这就是我想跟您谈谈的原因。我想多了解一下学法律是什么 样的。 3 M: A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion. Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree. The thing is there are many different branches of law and many different jobs. M: 在我看来，法律职业是一件美好的事情。很多人会说这是个枯燥的领域，但我不同意。事实是法律有 很多不同的分支，也有很多不同的工作。 4 W: You are involved with buildings and construction, right? W: 您是做建筑和施工方面的，对吧？ 5 M: Correct. I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes. M: 没错。我是一名律师，专攻房地产领域。我的大部分工作涉及调解土地纠纷。 6 W: Do you mind giving me an example? W: 您介意给我举个例子吗？ 7 M: Sure. So in many cases I am employed to arbitrate between two clashing parties. Let's say for example, there are two landowners who are in a thorny disagreement about something like the borders of Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. their adjacent plots. Someone may employ me to break the deadlock and resolve the dispute. Often my work involves negotiating agreements, plain and simple. M: 当然。在很多情况下，我受雇于在两个冲突方之间进行仲裁。比如说，有两个土地所有者在某件事上 存在棘手的分歧，比如他们相邻地块的边界问题。可能有人会雇用我来打破僵局，解决争端。我的工作通 常涉及协商协议，简单明了。 8 W: So you are saying that a lot of what you do is fix people's legal issues, like you try to find a solution that benefits everyone and that prevents a problem from escalating. W: 所以您是说，您做的很多工作是解决人们的法律问题，比如您试图找到一个对每个人都有利的解决方 案，防止问题升级。 9 M: Exactly, well put. You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible. M: 完全正确，说得好。你需要记住，法院和所有官僚机构一样，可能会非常混乱、令人沮丧，而且费用 昂贵。因此，只要有可能，最好在法庭外解决问题。 10 W: I see. W: 对。所以我一直在考虑学习刑法。我觉得听起来非常有趣。 13 M: Mm-hmm, yes. I'd say there's more money in property law, but the stakes are higher in criminal law. I can see how you would find it more interesting. M: 嗯，是的。我会说房地产法更赚钱，但刑法的风险更高。我能理解你为什么会觉得它更有趣。

analysis.text: You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible. 你要记住，法庭和所有官僚机构一样，可能非常混乱、令人沮丧而且昂贵。正因如此，能在 庭外解决问题通常更好。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果信号 For this reason。For this reason 是明确的因果连接词，它前面那句 courts...can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive 就是『为什么庭外解决更好』的 原因，顺着 For this reason 往前一句即定位到答案。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: frustrating, and expensive ↔Courts can be frustrating and expensive. 原词提取，去掉多余特征

analysis.text: B) 原词陷阱 The skill of preventing conflicts between parties concerned. 蹭了前文 prevents a problem from escalating 与调解纠纷的整段话题，听上去和这职业最贴；但题干问 any law professional 被要求的能力，录音对此的回答是 eloquent at articulating，不是预防 冲突，属答非所问的原词陷阱。 借用原文：prevents a problem from escalating A) 偷换概念 The ability to make arguments in a unique way. 借了录音 articulating that argument 的 argument，但录音只说要 eloquent(善于表达)，从未说要『以独特的方式』论辩， unique 是凭空加上的限定。 借用原文：articulating that argument C) 张冠李戴 The skill of foreseeing any potential stakes in their work. 盗用了结尾 the stakes are higher in criminal law 的 stakes，但那是男士比较两类法律时说的话，与『法律从业者被 要求的能力』无关，且录音从没说要『预见潜在利害』。 借用原文：the stakes are higher in criminal law Section B 1 When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information. But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories. 当一个人试图提取记忆时，他们的大脑会快速检查其中存储的所有内容以找到相关信息。但随着年龄增长, 我们中的许多人在提取记忆时会遇到困难。 2 In a review published in the journal *Trends in Cognitive Sciences* on February 11th, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories. While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides—this life experience can aid with creativity and decision-making. 在2月11日发表于《认知科学趋势》期刊的一篇综述中,研究人员提出了一种解释,说明为什么会发生这种情 况:老年人的大脑为积累的知识分配了更多空间,在试图提取记忆时有更多材料需要检索。虽然这种丰富的 先验知识可能会使记忆提取变得困难,但研究人员表示它也有其优势——这些人生经验可以帮助创造力和 决策。 3 Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it. Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context. 然而,关于幼儿如何学习什么值得努力的研究相对较少。我们都知道婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者,但他们 不只是无所事事地观看,他们是微小的学习机器。他们仅从几个例子就能概括出因果关系和社会角色等抽象 Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. 概念。即使是15个月大的婴儿在此类任务中也能胜过高级计算机。婴儿在涉及努力时是否也能从几个例子 中做出广泛的可概括推断?如果可以,那么也许坚持不懈并非单纯的性格特质,也许它是灵活的,可以根据社会 情境进行调整。 3 To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things—an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal. Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top. The button could be pressed down, but didn't actually activate anything. Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music. We gave the babies the music toy and left the room. Then analysts who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched video tapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button. 为了探索这个问题,我们向15个月大的婴儿展示两种情况之一——一个实验者努力工作以实现两个不同的 目标,或者一个实验者毫不费力地达成每个目标。然后我们向婴儿介绍一个新奇的音乐玩具,看起来似乎可 以通过按压顶部的大按钮来激活。这个按钮可以被按下,但实际上不会激活任何东西。在婴儿看不见的地 方,我们用一个隐藏按钮打开音乐玩具,让他们听到玩具发出音乐。我们把音乐玩具给婴儿,然后离开房间。 接着,不知道每个婴儿处于哪种条件的分析人员观看实验录像带,并计算婴儿尝试通过按压按钮来激活玩具 的次数。 4 Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed push the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed. In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding. Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions. Instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task. The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music. Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence. 在一项研究及一次预先注册的重复实验中,看到成人坚持并成功的婴儿按压按钮的次数大约是看到成人毫不 费力就成功的婴儿的两倍。换句话说,婴儿仅通过观看成人努力工作并成功的两个例子就学会了努力是有价 值的。这一发现令人兴奋的部分原因在于,婴儿不只是模仿成人的行为。相反,他们将努力的价值概括到了 一项新任务中。实验者从未演示过按压按钮或试图制造音乐。相反,婴儿从不同的努力行为例子中学到,这 个新玩具可能也需要坚持不懈。

analysis.text: A) 过度推断 Perform difficult tasks successfully just by observing how adults acted. 借了录音 keen observers / observing 的"观察"之意，但原文说的是婴儿从观察中"做出推断、推广 努力的价值"，并没说他们"光靠看就成功完成难任务"；successfully、just by 把原意夸大 了一截，是过度推断。 借用原文：infants are keen observers of the social world C) 偷换概念 Adapt themselves to different social contexts. 盗用录音 based on social context 的 social context，但原文是说"坚持也许是灵活的、随社会情境而变"（指坚持这一特质的性 质），不是说"婴儿能让自己适应不同社会情境"，主体和意思都被偷换。 借用原文：it's flexible and adaptable based on social context D) 张冠李戴 Work hard to interact with experimenters. 借了录音里反复出现的 experimenter（实验 者）和 effort / work hard 之意，但原文说"努力工作"的是录像里的成人 an adult working hard，婴儿是观察者，录音从没说婴儿"努力去和实验者互动"，是张冠李戴。 借用原文：an adult working hard 1 If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more. If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes. 如果长期迟到已经接管了你的生活并成为你的一个标志性特征,那么你很可能正在失去工作机会、娱乐机 会、友谊等等。如果你总是迟到于自己的人生,那就要组织好自己,优先考虑守时,并解决任何潜在的原因。 2 When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to. If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do. Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive. Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early. You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time. 当你必须去某个地方时,尽量在需要到达的时间前15到30分钟到达。如果你总是迟到,那意味着你肯定没有 把某些你总会做的事情考虑在内。通过给自己额外的时间到达来预见这一点。记录你是否真的提前到达 了。你可能会发现提前出发让你恰好准时到达目的地。 Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. 3 Set two alarms. Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door. Obey the alarms. As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you're doing. If it's something you'll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off. Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going. Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings. This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them. 设置两个闹钟。设置一个闹钟让你知道该放下手头的事情了,再设置第二个闹钟意味着你需要走出门。服从 闹钟。第一个闹钟一响,就停下你正在做的事情。如果是你会回来继续做的事情,比如工作项目,做个笔记提 醒自己做到哪里了。拿上你需要的所有东西,确保你知道如何到达目的地。争取在第二个闹钟响起之前出门 上路。这只有在你认真对待闹钟时才会奏效,所以确保你一听到闹钟就做出反应。 4 Prepare for the day ahead. If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before. Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day. 为即将到来的一天做好准备。提前把每个活动的所有笔记和材料整理好,这样到了真正的那天你只需要拿起 它们就走。如果早晨对你来说很困难,那就尽可能在前一晚做好准备。睡觉前,把第二天的衣服摆好,把包收 拾好。 5 Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. A) Librarians know the value of their community services, and their patrons appreciate their importance as well. But in an increasingly digital world, we see the role of libraries as community and cultural centers at times undervalued. When shrinking municipal budgets combine with the nonstop technological revolution, public library services that focus on building communities face-to-face, inspiring and educating patrons about art, literature, and music, and helping patrons engage in civil discourse can seem old-fashioned. But it is precisely those shrinking budgets and the assault of technologically mediated life that make public libraries' cultural and community offerings more important than ever.
B) Many people point out the value public libraries bring to their communities. More than just books and banks of computers, libraries are still places where individuals gather to explore, interact, and imagine. Some of the specific ways in which libraries add value to our communities and serve as cultural centers for our patrons are community builders, centers for the arts, and champions of youth. Libraries serve in these capacities and are more than just about information.
C) As community builders libraries are engaged in incredible work. From tiny public libraries to huge city institutions with multiple branches, libraries across the United States are building community and supporting local culture in exciting ways. These are inspiring and hopefully will encourage librarians interested in community services and cultural outreach to make connections with each other, share ideas, and build partnerships. Supporters of libraries as community builders claim that unless you are out there changing neighborhoods, you are not completing the work you are to do. Strengthening neighborhoods and championing the cultural lives of communities are big responsibilities.
D) Place-based economic development stresses the importance of offering attractive, functional, and community-based places, such as libraries, in town squares and depressed neighborhoods. Like a major department store in a mall, libraries attract large numbers of people, creating economic opportunities for numerous businesses and organizations in the surrounding area. Large cities, medium-sized ones, and even small towns have successfully transformed their libraries into the hubs(枢纽) of vibrant neighborhoods.
E) As key municipal agencies, and focal points for community education, libraries are major players in creating livable, environmentally friendly cities and towns. The Urban Libraries Council released a report detailing the unique ways in which libraries can further sustainability at the local level. Beyond ensuring that library construction projects consider environmental impact, libraries can take a lead in supporting local foods and craftsmen, like the Peabody Institute Library's partnering with local businesses to pioneer a farmers' market in their courtyard, or the Richmond Public Library's seed lending library which "nurtures locally-adapted plant varieties, and fosters community resilience(韧性), self-reliance and a culture of sharing."
F) Archives preserve historic artifacts, oral histories, digital history projects, and scholarly writings relevant to the community, including minority groups. Communities lucky enough to have archivists have a great advantage when it comes to organizing historical records and artifacts. An organized archive is a place where people can research their ancestry and immigration history, do environmental research, and more. An archivist is an advocate for preservation who, among other things, coordinates the restoration of maps and paintings, the digitization of vital records, and the creation of oral history projects. With projects like the Massachussets Memories Road Show and the Veterans History Project, evidence of the importance of archives is everywhere.
G) In the words of Robert Putnam, "People may go to the library looking mainly for information, but they find each other there." New moms connect at baby story-times; elderly people, often facing difficult life transitions, attend events and find that they make new friends; teenagers meet up in libraries' teen spaces after school; and readers discuss current events in the periodicals room. In libraries, community-building connections are happening all the time.
H) As Keith Richards said, "The public library is the great equalizer." Despite the rising costs of concert and theater tickets, public library events (including concerts, author visits, and gallery displays) are often offered free of charge, enabling people of any income level to attend. In addition, library book groups allow people to explore and discuss the literary arts, and the Great Stories Club introduces at- risk youth to literature. The best part: it's all free and open to the public.
I) In a time when education is increasingly expensive, public libraries provide information and educational opportunities free for all people, regardless of their socio-economic status. Offered by libraries across the country, American Library Association's Let's Talk about It programs are wonderful examples of scholar-facilitated learning opportunities in libraries. In addition, many libraries present classes and discussion programs, and some even provide online continuing education courses such as the Universal Class database.
J) Librarians know that patrons aren't just information consumers, they're information producers. Patrons use the library to gain knowledge in order to create their own new and independent works. Increasing numbers of libraries provide spaces and services that meet the needs of people who want to learn how to edit Wikipedia, set up blogs or podcasts, create their own magazines, and so much more. Many libraries offer art or writing workshops and groups, and some provide music practice rooms for patrons. Programs like ImaginOn in Charlotte, North Carolina, provide exciting models that take community partnership, creativity, and creation to a new level.
K) The decline of civil discourse stems in part from the fact that it is so easy for people to watch news about, buy products from, and engage—in both the virtual and real worlds—only with those of similar backgrounds and ideologies. Public libraries, through such programs as The Human Library and Socrates Café, can help build small communities of difference that encourage people to interact with and learn from each other through dialogue. By both actively promoting civil discourse through these programs, and modeling and upholding the principles of free inquiry and expression for all, libraries help individuals rediscover the importance of and increased need for civil discourse in American life.
L) Free tutoring, homework help programs, and summer reading programs for kids and teens help bridge the economic divide that impacts students' academic performance. The cost of hiring a private tutor is well beyond what many library patrons can afford, so libraries offer homework help and tutoring online, by phone, in person, and even through social media and homework apps. Annual summer reading programs also have a positive impact on student performance and, according to a 2010 study conducted by Dominican University's Graduate School of Library and Information Science, students' reading skills get a boost from these popular nationwide events.
M) Through library collections, programs, and physical spaces, children learn to share, to be engaged in their communities, to participate in the arts, and to explore their immediate world and the world at large. There are surely endless examples of innovative library services for children, including the Middle Country Public Library's Nature Explorium, which engages children in learning about the natural world.

P1 After earning a bachelor's degree, I was determined to do what I love. I headed straight to graduate school to investigate the social problems that fascinated me.

P2 For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later."

P3 It wasn't until I began to research this widely accepted career advice that I understood how problematic it really was.

P4 As a sociologist, I interviewed college students and professional workers to learn what it really meant to pursue their dreams, which I will refer to here as the passion principle. I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book. Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.

P5 Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision-making priority. And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability.

P6 Advocates of the passion principle found it compelling because they believed that following one's passion can provide workers with both the motivation necessary to work hard and a place to find fulfillment.

P7 Yet, what I found is that following one's passion does not necessarily lead to fulfillment, but is one of the most powerful cultural forces perpetuating overwork. I also found that promoting the pursuit of one's passion helps perpetuate social inequalities due to the fact that not everyone has the same economic resources to allow them to pursue their passion with ease.

P8 While the passion principle is broadly popular, not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good-paying job. Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs. Surveys revealed that working-class and first-generation college graduates, regardless of their career field, are more likely than their wealthier peers to end up in low-paying unskilled jobs when they pursue their passion.

P9 Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.

P10 It's not just well-off passion-seekers who benefit from the passion principle. Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay. They even sacrifice a good salary, job stability and leisure time to work in a job they love.

P11 B) People are less concerned with socioeconomic inequality 说人们对不平等的关注度 C) help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities ↔Socioeconomic inequality is likely to persist D)

P12 C) They level the playing field for these workers to reach their goals 把『拉平起跑 D) They encourage these workers to realize their aspirations 用『鼓励员工实现抱负』

P1 Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year. Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction.

P2 These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. In 2015, the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.

P3 Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. After all, if students don't show up, teachers can't teach them.

P4 But what if America's attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face—such as being ejected Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?

P5 As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children's academic achievement.

P6 We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning. In fact, children with no unexcused absences—but 15 to 18 excused absences—have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences.

P7 Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.

P8 We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children's academic progress.

P9 Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.

P10 How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy. School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences.

P11 These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction. They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. We find neither to be the case.

P12 As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often.

P13 We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.

blocks.label: P2
blocks.text: These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. In 2015, the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.

blocks.label: P3
blocks.text: Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. After all, if students don't show up, teachers can't teach them.

blocks.label: P4
blocks.text: But what if America's attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face—such as being ejected Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?

blocks.label: P5
blocks.text: As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children's academic achievement.

blocks.label: P6
blocks.text: We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning. In fact, children with no unexcused absences—but 15 to 18 excused absences—have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences.

blocks.label: P7
blocks.text: Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.

blocks.label: P8
blocks.text: We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children's academic progress.

blocks.label: P9
blocks.text: Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.

blocks.label: P10

blocks.label: P11

blocks.label: P12
blocks.text: As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often.

blocks.label: P13
blocks.text: We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.

writing.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "As requirements for job applications are getting increasingly higher, college students ought to be better prepared for their future career." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words. You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
writing.model: As requirements for job applications are getting increasingly higher, college students ought to be better prepared for their future career. In an era when employers demand not only a diploma but also practical competence, waiting until graduation to think about work is simply too late. There are concrete steps every student can take. To begin with, obtaining relevant certificates and mastering professional skills builds a solid foundation. Last summer, for instance, I taught myself data analysis and earned a certificate, which later helped me stand out in an internship interview. What is more, internships offer irreplaceable experience: by working in a real company, students learn how a workplace actually operates and discover which career truly suits them. Such preparation turns abstract knowledge into employable ability. In conclusion, the fiercer competition becomes, the more valuable early preparation is. Therefore, college students should seize every chance to enrich their skills and experience, so that when opportunity knocks, they are ready to open the door.

translation.source: 天宫空间站(Tiangong Space Station)是中国首个太空实验室,拥有110多立方米使用空间,可驻留三名宇航员,在距地球表面400-450公里的轨道上运行。天宫空间站已实施180多个科学研究与应用项目,涉及空间生命科学、太空医学、空间材料科学等领域。天宫空间站的研究成果在我国得到了广泛应用,产生了显著的经济效益。例如,太空育种创造的直接经济效益高达数千亿元。这不仅标志中国在航天技术上取得了巨大进步,也表明中国为全球的太空研究和应用做出了重大贡献。
translation.reference: The Tiangong Space Station, China's first space laboratory, boasts over 110 cubic meters of usable space and is able to accommodate three astronauts, orbiting at an altitude of 400 to 450 kilometers above the Earth's surface. The station has carried out more than 180 scientific research and application projects, covering such fields as space life science, space medicine, and space materials science. The research achievements of the station have been widely applied in China and have generated remarkable economic benefits. For example, the direct economic benefits created by space breeding reach hundreds of billions of yuan. This not only marks China's tremendous progress in aerospace technology, but also demonstrates that China has made significant contributions to global space research and application.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：天宫空间站是中国首个太空实验室（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已有明确主语"天宫空间站"，天宫空间站(Tiangong Space Station)是中国首个太空实验室 这 一判断句最适合立为主干：主语 Tiangong Space Station，系动词 is，表语 China's first space laboratory。后面"拥有…""可驻留…""在…轨道上运行"都是对它的进一步描述，不必各起一句。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 三个并列描述降级为分词与介词短语 主干外有三个动词性成分需降级："拥有110多立方米使用空间" 现在分词短语 with over 110 cubic meters of usable space 或 boasting…；"可驻留三名宇航员"→ able to accommodate three astronauts（形容词短语）或并入分词；"在距地球表面400-450公里的轨道上运行" 现在 分词 orbiting at an altitude of 400 to 450 kilometers above the Earth's surface。三者用分词/ 介词短语挂在主干后，而不是用三个 and 平铺成流水句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 回指全篇基调用一般现在时：is / accommodate / orbiting 都表持续存在的事实。 单复数 三名宇航员 不止一名→ three astronauts 用复数；cubic meters、kilometers 是计量复数也须加 s。 数字范围与介词搭配 "110多"→ over / more than 110；"400-450公里"用 from 400 to 450 kilometers 或 400 to 450 kilometers；"距地球表面"用 above the Earth's surface，"在轨道上运行"用 orbit at an altitude of… 搭配。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Tiangong Space Station, China's first space laboratory, boasts over 110 cubic meters of usable space and is able to accommodate three astronauts, orbiting at an altitude of 400 to 450 kilometers above the Earth's surface. 2. 天宫空间站已实施180多个科学研究与应用项目,涉及空间生命科学、太空医学、空间材料科学 等领域。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：天宫空间站已实施180多个项目（主语策略：原句主语） 主语仍是"天宫空间站"，核心动作是 已实施180多个科学研究与应用项目 中的"实施"→ has carried out / has conducted，宾语 over 180 scientific research and application projects。"涉及…等领域"是对这些项目的补充说明，降级处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 涉及领域降级为分词定语 "涉及空间生命科学、太空医学、空间材料科学等领域"修饰前面的 projects，降级为现在分词短语 作后置定语：covering / involving fields such as space life science, space medicine, and space materials science。"等领域"用 such as…、…and so on 或 fields including… 处理，不必 把"等"硬译成 etc. 堆在句尾。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "已实施"是已完成并对现状有影响的动作，偏离基调用现在完成时 has carried out / has conducted，与全篇"截至目前已取得的成果"语境一致。 单复数与主谓一致 180多个…项目→ over 180 projects 复数；主语 Station 单数，故助动词用 has（不是 have）。 并列与冠词 三个学科领域并列用逗号 + and 连接，最后一项前加 and；学科名 space life science 等作不可数 抽象领域名，一般不加冠词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The station has carried out more than 180 scientific research and application projects, covering such fields as space life science, space medicine, and space materials science. 3. 天宫空间站的研究成果在我国得到了广泛应用,产生了显著的经济效益。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：研究成果已被广泛应用（主语策略：转被动） 研究成果在我国得到了广泛应用 中"研究成果"是"应用"这一动作的承受者，中文用"得到了…应 用"本身就是被动语义，故转被动：主语 The research achievements，谓语 have been widely applied。后半"产生了显著的经济效益"承接同一主语，作并列谓语。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两个谓语并列，状语降级 本句主干较简单："得到了广泛应用"和"产生了显著的经济效益"是同一主语的两个并列动作，用 and 连接两个谓语（have been widely applied … and have generated significant economic benefits）。"在我国"是地点状语，降级为介词短语 in China 放句末或谓语后。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 语态 "得到了广泛应用"用被动 have been applied；"产生了经济效益"主语"成果"是主动产生，用主动 have generated。一句内被动 + 主动并存，须分别判断。 时态 "得到了""产生了"均为已完成动作，用现在完成时 have been applied / have generated，回指本 篇"已取得成果"的语境。 单复数 主语 achievements 复数 助动词用 have；benefits 经济效益作可数复数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The research achievements of the station have been widely applied in China and have generated remarkable economic benefits. 4. 例如,太空育种创造的直接经济效益高达数千亿元。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：直接经济效益高达数千亿元（主语策略：原句主语） 本句核心是"经济效益 + 高达 + 数千亿元"，太空育种创造的直接经济效益高达数千亿元 中以"直接 经济效益"作主语，谓语 reach / amount to，宾语 hundreds of billions of yuan。"太空育种创 造的"是修饰主语的定语，"例如"是衔接词单独处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 创造的降级为过去分词定语，例如转衔接副词 "太空育种创造的"修饰"经济效益"，降级为过去分词短语作后置定语 created by space breeding；"例如"不是句子成分，是承接上句的衔接词，译为 For example / For instance 置于 句首加逗号。整句：For example, the direct economic benefits created by space breeding reach hundreds of billions of yuan.

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 数字表达 "数千亿元"→ hundreds of billions of yuan（亿 = hundred million，千亿 = hundred billion；"数千亿"用 hundreds of billions）。货币单位 yuan 作复数计量时一般不加 s。 时态 陈述这一既成数值事实，可用一般现在时 reach（表目前已达到的水平），与上下文"已取得的成 果"也相容；用一般过去时 reached 亦可，本篇建议跟现状统一用 reach。 单复数与冠词 benefits 复数 谓语 reach；特指上文提到的这类效益，主语前用 the direct economic benefits。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: For example, the direct economic benefits created by space breeding reach hundreds of billions of yuan. 5. 这不仅标志中国在航天技术上取得了巨大进步,也表明中国为全球的太空研究和应用做出了重 大贡献。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 主干：这既标志…也表明…（主语策略：原句主语） 主语"这"指代前文整件事，译为 This；这不仅标志中国…也表明中国… 是 not only…but also… 关 联的两个并列谓语：not only marks… but also demonstrates / shows…。两个 that 宾语从句分 别承载"取得进步"和"做出贡献"。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两动作用that从句承接，并列谓语 "标志""表明"译为两个并列谓语 marks / demonstrates，各带一个 that 宾语从句：that China has made great progress in aerospace technology / that China has made significant contributions to global space research and application。用 not only … but also … 连接，体 现递进。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 从句"取得了巨大进步""做出了重大贡献"是已完成动作，用现在完成时 has made；主句"标志""表 明"是对当前事实的陈述，用一般现在时 marks / demonstrates。主从时态各依语义，不必一律。 主谓一致 主语 This 单数 谓语 marks / demonstrates 加 s；从句主语 China 单数→ has made。 介词搭配 "在航天技术上取得进步"→ make progress in aerospace technology；"为…做出贡献"→ make contributions to global space research and application，contribute to 的搭配介词是 to，不 是 for。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: This not only marks China's tremendous progress in aerospace technology, but also demonstrates that China has made significant contributions to global space research and application. 英语六级 2025年6月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
